findings.title: Phpinfo Use
findings.description: The phpinfo() function is used to output information about PHP's configuration, which can reveal sensitive information about the environment, such as file paths and database credentials. By removing this function call, the sensitive information is no longer disclosed. This fix assumes that the phpinfo() call was not intended for production use, but rather for debugging purposes.
findings.cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.fix_hint: Remove the phpinfo() function call to prevent information disclosure

findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the SQL query. Using prepared statements with parameter binding ensures that user input is treated as data, not as part of the SQL code. This prevents an attacker from injecting malicious SQL code and reduces the risk of data theft or manipulation.
findings.cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities

attack_chains.title: SQLi to RCE
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses SQL injection to extract database credentials, then uses these credentials to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec vulnerability, achieving persistence on the system. This chain requires minimal skill and results in critical data loss. The attacker starts by exploiting a SQL injection vulnerability in the low.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses SQL injection in vulnerabilities/sqli/source/low.php (id: cc6c942f) to extract database credentials
Step 2: this gives them access to the database, which they use to gain remote code execution via a tainted exec vulnerability in vulnerabilities/exec/source/low.php (id: 0cf55e24)
attack_chains.remediation: Input validation and sanitization on user input to prevent SQL injection

attack_chains.title: Phpinfo to SQLi
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a phpinfo page to discover database configuration details, then uses this information to exploit a SQL injection vulnerability, potentially extracting sensitive data. This chain requires minimal skill and results in significant data loss. The attacker starts by accessing the phpinfo.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker accesses phpinfo.php (id: eeeeecc3b) to discover database configuration details
Step 2: this gives them the information needed to exploit a SQL injection vulnerability in vulnerabilities/bac/source/low.php (id: d1e9b83a)
attack_chains.remediation: Remove or restrict access to the phpinfo.php page to prevent information disclosure

attack_chains.title: Tainted Exec to Persistence
attack_chains.description: An attacker uses a tainted exec vulnerability to gain remote code execution, then uses this access to achieve persistence on the system. This chain requires moderate skill and results in significant system compromise. The attacker starts by exploiting a tainted exec vulnerability in the high.php file.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses a tainted exec vulnerability in vulnerabilities/exec/source/high.php (id: 91c70ff4) to gain remote code execution
Step 2: this gives them the ability to achieve persistence on the system by creating a new user or modifying system files
attack_chains.remediation: Implement proper input validation and sanitization on user input to prevent command injection
